synthesis.verdict: Not yet. Rev D's analysis is careful and reproduces exactly from a clean snapshot of f4d20e3: members 0.96, joints 0.89, links 0.68. But four things fail when the parts are checked as they would actually be built, so Rev D should not go to a registered engineer for adoption until they are fixed. (1) The 22 truss joints inside the cradles are credited with gussets that cannot be fitted there. With the 4 screws actually present, 18 of them are over capacity, up to 1.73. (2) The lip-notch check uses the full section for bending and skips tension. Done properly, the wall tracks reach 1.17 and the 1.15 mm edge-truss chords sit at 0.99 even at first yield, and go over 1.0 once local buckling of the cut flange is allowed. (3) The lifting head's sideways check assumes a closed box. The drawn head is two 3 mm cheeks, which fail out of plane at the model's own 5 % sideways force (about 1.3-1.9). (4) Hold point H5 accepts drops up to 15 % off their design share, while a twist of about 4-6 % already reaches capacity. Fix those first. Then: settle one drop-lean limit and one CoG and pick-setting accuracy budget, because tilt plus lean and the CoG corners have little or no margin; move the four south feet that hit the truss-end cleats; draw full-depth cleats, real gusset and bolt layouts and a buildable head; put the 1.15 mm gauge into the saved Framer job; make the in-service support rule realistic; and bring the design basis up from Rev C. With those done it is a reasonable package for an engineer to review. As it stands, an engineer would send it back. The repository has since moved on to cf80b19, with changes that touch some of these points; those changes were not reviewed here.

blocking.title: Cradle joints are credited with gussets that cannot be fitted; with the screws actually there, 18 joints are over capacity
blocking.lenses: Capacity and connectors; Buildability and the Framer model
blocking.evidence: run_lift.py:617 gives every joint in gusset_joints 10 screw-equivalents. 22 of the 24 bottom-chord joints inside the 12 cradle footprints are in that list; size_joints.py picked them because they exceed 0.90 at 4 screws. The config note (revD_final.json:223) says the cradle cheek is the gusset there, but the cheek drawn in tools/add_lift_components.py:78-84 runs from z -410 to -250. That is only about 9 mm above the top of the edge-truss bottom chord (about -300 to -259), so it cannot take 3 screws into each web member, and by design it is screwed at the first joint only (revD_final.json:177). add_lift_components.py:139-141 also draws 22 LIFT_GU plates on the same faces as the cheeks: both cannot be fitted, and the BOQ counts the plates. Re-run: I solved the 15 design cases from a git-archive of f4d20e3 and re-checked those joints at the 4 screws actually there (2 Framer screws with end rupture plus 2 added, 1.15 mm). 18 of 24 exceed 1.0. Worst: N4h bearing-only seat at x 11100, 13.28 kN against 7.66 kN = 1.73 (reported 0.65, R1). Then N1h screwed seat at x 899, 13.59 against 8.49 = 1.60 (R1); S3a bearing seat at x 7131, 10.52 against 7.66 = 1.37 (L4); S1a at x 516, 1.32 (L3); N2h at x 4485, 1.29 (T6). Without R1 it is still 18 over (max 1.73 in T1). Even counting the 4 cheek screws as joint screws at the screwed seats leaves the 10 bearing-only joints at 1.11-1.73.
blocking.fix: Give both joints of every pair a real screwed gusset. One way: a 1.5 mm plate under each cheek, fitted before the cradle (cheek gap and sleeve about 98 mm, clearance holes for the plate screws). Another: a cheek extended at least about 70 mm above the chord, with 3 screws into each web member and 3 into the chord per face, at both joints. Model those screws and re-check the cheek screws, bearing bolts and seats. Otherwise set n = 4 at the cradle joints and strengthen (heavier webs, or a cradle that bears on the webs). Remove the 22 overlapping LIFT_GU plates from the BOQ and the IFC.

blocking.title: Lip-notch check uses full-section bending and skips tension; checked with the notched section, the tracks exceed 1.0 and the 1.15 mm edge-truss chords have no margin
blocking.lenses: Frame model and load path; Capacity and connectors
blocking.evidence: liftcase.py:127 reduces only the axial capacity at a notch. Lines 130-131 compute phiMx and phiMy for the full lipped section, and line 146 uses them in the notch interaction. The notch branch runs only for N < 0 (lines 141-147), so tension plus bending at a notch is checked on the full section. Without the lips, the minor-axis modulus at the flange tips drops from 1,258 to 729 mm3 at 0.95 mm (Iy 33,146 to 21,171 mm4). Phi times first yield is then 0.295 kNm against the 0.363 used (0.81); at 1.15 mm it is 0.352 against 0.493 (0.72). Re-check: all 161 notched members at element ends within 25 mm of a notch, notched properties for every term, first yield only (the most favourable model). W4 bottom track 1.17 (reported 0.96, T6_SE, N -2.1 kN, Min 0.317 kNm); W1 bottom track 1.11; W4 stud 1.01. NFT2 top chord (1.15 mm, x 7738, T5_SW, tension 17.2 kN plus Min 0.26 kNm) 0.99 (reported 0.79). W1/W4 top tracks 0.97/0.96; NFT1 top chord 0.93; NFT2/NFT1 bottom chords 0.89/0.87. With local buckling of the cut flange (finite strip run on the unlipped section with the repo's FiniteStrip class, then DSM, re-run here), phiMy drops to 0.251/0.188 kNm at 0.95 mm and 0.340/0.258 kNm at 1.15 mm (web / tips in compression). That puts the edge-truss chords over 1.0. The notch buckling coefficient also assumes a 50 mm notch with supported ends (as4600.py:52 and 136). At joint pairs only about 27 mm of lip is left between two notches; with a = 127 mm the notched axial term rises 14 % (NFT4 top chord: axial term 0.66 to 0.75). Caveat: much of the track moment comes from the track spanning 210 mm between discrete links with a stud load between them, while the real track bears on the edge-truss chord. The chord moments are real truss action at the joint pairs.
blocking.fix: At notch stations, use notched-section properties for the axial term, both bending terms and tension (net area without the lips). Use an effective width or a finite-strip value for the unlipped flange, and take the notch length from the roll-former tooling (combined length at joint pairs, unless the nested web is shown to restrain the flange). Model the wall bottom tracks bearing on the edge-truss chord (compression-only contact at each stud) before relying on track moments. Re-check. If the NFT1/NFT2 chords near the lift lines reach 1.0, use a heavier gauge, a reinforcing plate or a zone with no notches.

blocking.title: Lifting-head sideways check uses a closed box the drawn head does not have; the 3 mm cheeks fail out of plane
blocking.lenses: Capacity and connectors (confirmed with a synthesis frame model)
blocking.evidence: run_connectors.py:136 and 148-149 check 10.5 % of the 23.66 kN factored sling force on a 170 mm cantilever against Z = 2(89 x 3^2/6 + 3 x 89^2/6) = 8,188 mm3, giving utilisation 0.13. The head drawn in add_lift_components.py:50-57 is two flat 3 mm cheeks, 120 x 450, on the truss faces, plus a top plate and the M20 pin along y. It has no end plates. A sideways force across the module therefore loads the cheeks out of plane. One 120 x 3 cheek has phiM 0.073 kNm elastic (0.109 kNm plastic). A simple U-frame model gives a cheek moment of about 121 mm x F: cheeks fixed into the pin/top-plate ring, bearing on the top chord on one side and the bottom chord on the other, pin at z 3090 as drawn. At the model's own factored guide shear in L1/L2 (1.13 kN): 0.137 kNm, utilisation 1.88 elastic / 1.26 plastic. At 2 deg, i.e. 3.5 % or 0.83 kN (about the 0.82 kN that tilt case T2 already puts on the head): 1.38 / 0.92. At the check's own 10.5 % (2.48 kN): 4.1 / 2.8. With the model's pin height (head_z 3150) it is about twice as bad. The north stop block, which takes the along-module force, is not drawn or checked.
blocking.fix: Redesign the head for out-of-plane load. Close the box with end plates, or fold stiffening returns down the cheeks above the truss, or use thicker cheeks or a gusseted lug. Keep the sling central with spacers on the sleeve. Check the cheeks as plates for the full sideways allowance in both directions. Draw and check the north stop block.

blocking.title: H5 lets the lift continue with drops up to 15 % off share, but a twist of 4-6 % already reaches capacity
blocking.evidence: H5 (docs/DESIGN_BASIS.md:69, report/make_report.py:268, site/index.html:1697) says: stop if any drop is more than 15 % from its design share. Rev D moved R7d (10 % twist) to information only (run_lift.py:513-516; skew_in_envelope false), yet R7d gives joints 1.54 and members 1.16. The four transverse beams are set separately, so opposite pick errors d on the west and east beams twist the module without tilting it. The hang angle is 0.02 deg, so the 2 deg level check cannot see it. Re-run of the twist patterns (cascade statics per line, factor 2.433): d = 75 mm gives joints 0.96 and members 0.95; d = 100 mm gives joints 1.13 and members 1.02. Capacity is at about d = 80 mm, a shift of about 0.40 kN per line at rated load: about 4 % of a south drop and 6 % of a north drop. H5 therefore accepts errors 2-3 times what the frame can take. No pick-setting tolerance is stated anywhere. And because a cascade imposes its own shares, H5 cannot see a twist in the module's own mass distribution at all.
blocking.fix: Set each transverse beam from its own line's south/north split, measured by the 8 H1 load cells, not from one global CoG. State a pick-setting tolerance (the load-case reviewer found that +/-50 mm keeps joints at or below 0.83). Add a twist design case at that tolerance. Set the H5 stop at about +/-4 % of each drop's design share.

should_fix.title: The drop-lean allowance has three values and is never combined with the 2 deg tilt; L1/L2 are not in equilibrium
should_fix.lenses: Frame model and load path; Load cases, rigging and in-service
should_fix.evidence: The basis and lift plan say drops within 2 deg, i.e. 3.5 % (DESIGN_BASIS.md:19, make_report.py:273). Frame cases L1-L4 use 5 % (revD_final.json:77, run_lift.py:535-547). The head check uses 10.5 %, labelled '6 deg drop tolerance' (run_connectors.py:136 and 148), which review.json:127 calls the single sideways fraction. Tilt cases T1-T8 carry no lean. Re-run: L4 at 10.5 % gives members 1.06 (NFT1 bottom chord, x 6000) and joints 1.17 (10 over); L3 at 10.5 % gives joints 1.14 (12 over) and link shear 0.89. 2 deg tilt plus 5 % lean: 5 of 32 combinations go over 1.0 (T3+L4 joints 1.045 at the NFT1 web at x 10384; T7+L4 1.040; T8+L4 1.030; T4+L4 1.022; T8+L3 1.013), and members reach 0.99. At the basis value (2 deg tilt with 3.5 % lean) it passes at the design CoG: 0.98 members, 0.97 joints. L1/L2 apply 5 % of each head's own force (south 9.3 kN, north 6.7 kN). That leaves 0.53 kN across the module at rated load, which only the artificial holds take (unbalance 263.6 N per hold in summary.json; liftcase.py:53-54 says it should be about 0).
should_fix.fix: Adopt one drop-lean limit. 2 deg fits the rig if the drop spacing equals the 3,211 mm head spacing within a stated tolerance. Use that limit in both the frame cases and the head check, and run the tilt x lean combinations as design cases (re-size the gussets with them). Apply the sideways forces on each transverse beam as equal and opposite pairs. If 5 % or 6 deg is kept, strengthen the NFT1 web joints, the chords and the seats.

should_fix.title: H1 does not control what the design assumes: the CoG envelope corners and the pick-setting accuracy use up the margin
should_fix.evidence: H1 allows the CoG within 90 mm across and 150 mm along of the design position (review.json:61). At the corners one drop rises 9.5-11.6 % by cascade statics, more than the 1.05 CoG factor covers. Explicit corner runs (masses re-weighted, cascade set at the new CoG, CoG factor 1.0): at (+150, -90) joints 0.971 (T3, NFT1 web at x 6467), re-run here; at (+150, +90) members 0.994 (T6, W4 bottom track), from the load-case reviewer's run. Adding 2 deg lean at the corners gives members 1.012 and joints 1.030. Tilt margin: 2 deg is only 67 mm of pick offset (h = 1,916 mm). Re-run tilt sweep: 2.5 deg gives members 1.03 (T6) and joints 1.03 (T2, NFT3 web); 3 deg gives 1.09 and 1.20. Capacity is therefore at about 2.3 deg, or about 77 mm. No accuracy is stated for the load cells, the pick setting or the level check at the trial lift (make_report.py:274). The drop WLL is taken at the design CoG (1.07 t); at the corners it is about 1.12 t.
should_fix.fix: Derive the H1 limit from the analysis. Run the corners with the tilt and tilt x lean cases at CoG factor 1.0, and tighten H1 until they pass (a starting point is about +/-60 mm across and +/-100 mm along), or strengthen the governing NFT1 web joints. State an accuracy budget for the load cells, the pick setting and the level instrument, and a measured stop criterion at the trial lift. Take the drop WLL from the envelope (at least 1.12 t).

should_fix.title: Four south feet (S1a, S2b, S3a, S4b) do not fit: strap and cheek hit the truss-end cleats, and the M16 bearing bolts are 15-22 mm from the cheek end
should_fix.lenses: Frame model and load path; Buildability and the Framer model
should_fix.evidence: gap() (run_lift.py:164-167) measures clearance only to the bare 89 mm floor-truss end. The same design puts a 50 mm cleat leg on each side of every truss end on the inner face (add_lift_components.py:91-94 and 142-148: x = t +/- 46.5 to 96.5, z -250 to -50, in the plane y 89-90.5). That is the same plane as the inner strap (y 89-90.2). Measured along each strap path: the inner straps of S1a, S2b, S3a and S4b overlap the cleat legs of the trusses at x 600, 4800, 7200 and 11400 by 33.0-33.7 mm, where summary.json reports strap gaps of 14.3-15.1 mm. Their inner cheeks overlap the legs in plan by 35-43 mm, and the cheek top (z -250) meets the leg bottom (z -250). The other four feet clear by 64-80 mm. seat_edge 15 (revD_final.json:244; place_cradle, run_lift.py:186-195) puts the M16 bolts of S2b and S3a 14.9 and 15.0 mm from the cheek end, and those of S1a and S4b 22.0 and 21.9 mm. All four are below 1.5d = 24 mm even before allowing for the larger sleeve hole. S2b and S3a cannot be lengthened, because the truss end is 8.7-8.8 mm away. run_connectors.py:123 checks tear-out downwards only.
should_fix.fix: Add the cleat legs and their screw heads to gap(). Set seat_edge from the sleeve hole (about 35-40 mm). Move the four feet, or use a cleat on the far side only at those four truss ends and re-check the end reaction. Add an edge-distance check to run_connectors.py, then re-run.

should_fix.title: Truss-end cleats as drawn do not reach the edge-truss chords
should_fix.lenses: Capacity and connectors; Buildability and the Framer model
should_fix.evidence: The cleat check credits 5 screws per leg into the edge truss (run_connectors.py:154-160; revD_final.json:147), and the model ties the end reaction into the edge-truss chord nodes (framemodel.py:312-329). The drawn leg (add_lift_components.py:91-94) is 200 mm tall and centred at mid-depth. Floor legs run from z -250 to -50, while the chords are at about -300 to -259 and -41 to 0, so the legs stop about 9 mm short of both chords; roof legs are similar. Only parts of the Warren diagonals lie behind a leg. The corner-truss legs at x -52 to -2 and 12,002 to 12,052 are outside the module. The build reviewer's screw packing study (not re-run here) found that 100 of the 168 legs cannot take 5 screws and 52 can take none. In service, four ends then fail on the screws that do fit (1.21-1.60); in the lift the ends still pass (0.77).
should_fix.fix: Make the cleat a full-depth angle (about 280 mm), screwed into both chord flanges and the truss end vertical. Combine it with the end gusset where both are needed, and make a corner version for the end trusses. Re-run the link and in-service checks with the real screw counts.

should_fix.title: Gusset detail: the 10-screw-equivalent credit has no plate layout, and the drawn plates cannot be installed
should_fix.lenses: Capacity and connectors; Buildability and the Framer model
should_fix.evidence: The joint check credits (2 min(c1, er) + 8 c1) x 0.9 = 20.39 / 21.22 kN at 1.15 mm (15.57 / 15.93 kN at 0.95 mm). That is 4 joint screws plus 6 plate screws, all at full capacity, which needs 3d spacing and 1.5d edges in a plate that also clears the dimple screws and the nested web ends. The drawn plate (add_lift_components.py:86-89, placed at 139-141) is 100 x 100 and centred on the node. At the 113 top-chord gussets it therefore stands 29.5 mm above the truss top, into the floor sheet and under the wall tracks. 63 pairs of plates on the same face are only 51.9-58.1 mm apart and overlap (12 of these pairs are at NFT1/NFT2 joint pairs), and 22 plates sit on the cradle cheeks (see the cradle blocking finding). The plate pair itself is strong enough: 27.7 kN with a 35 mm Whitmore width, against 13.6 kN.
should_fix.fix: Issue a dimensioned gusset detail: one plate per joint pair, flush with the chord's outer face, with screw positions and edge distances that clear the dimple screws. Keep the 10-equivalent credit only where that layout is shown to fit. Regenerate the components and the BOQ.

should_fix.title: Lifting-head detailing: the sling cannot reach the sleeve, the head is not seated, and pin bending is not checked
should_fix.lenses: Load cases, rigging and in-service; Buildability and the Framer model
should_fix.evidence: The drawn head has a closed 120 x 101 x 3 top plate at z 3147-3150, above the pin (add_lift_components.py:51-57). Yet the lift plan puts the shackle or sling eye over the sleeve inside the head (make_report.py:273; review.json:79). Nothing seats the head vertically: with slack slings it can drop about 70 mm until the sleeve lands on the roof truss, kinking the 1.2 / 1.5 mm straps. Pin bending is not checked, although the M16 cradle bolt is (run_connectors.py:117-120). For the M20 pin, 23.8 kN over 98 mm between cheek centres gives 0.29-0.58 kNm against phiMp 0.77 kNm on a plain shank (utilisation 0.38-0.76), or 1.25 if the thread runs into the span. '40 mm sleeve' does not say whether that is the diameter or the length. Per the build reviewer, 4 joint-screw heads per face (5-6 mm tall) sit under each cheek, which has only 3 mm running clearance; the joint-pair positions match the floor edge truss. The inner cheek and straps rise 150 mm above the roof truss, through battens and sheeting. The pin height is 3090 as drawn, 3150 in the model (head_z), and a 170 mm lever in the check.
should_fix.fix: Detail an open or slotted top with protected edges, or a shackle through the cheeks with the sling in the bow. Add a seat that holds the head at height without putting vertical load into the roof. Specify a plain-shank pin and add the bending check. State the sleeve size against the sling maker's minimum bearing diameter. Clear the screw heads (pads or wafer heads). Fix one pin height for the model, the checks and the component. Detail the roof cut-outs and flashing.

should_fix.title: Strap-end bolt layouts at the cradle and the head are not drawn, and do not fit where the parts are drawn
should_fix.lenses: Buildability and the Framer model; Frame model and load path
should_fix.evidence: The cradle cheeks sit flat on the chord faces (add_lift_components.py:82), so a strap bolt above the chord underside has no room for a nut. Below the chord, the M16 bearing bolts sit at about z -312 under the joints. At S1a the strap spans x 453.7-503.7 and the first bearing bolt is at x 458.2 with a 30 mm washer, so the strap would ride over a bolt head standing 13-16 mm proud. At the head, the two 50 mm A-frame straps overlap for the top ~195 mm (half angle 7.3 deg) and can only be bolted above the truss top, where the pin is. The connector rows (2 x M12 per strap end, utilisation 0.20) are not based on any drawn layout. The seat split also depends on the strap's line of action: the model reviewer found that moving it 60 mm higher lifts the S3a bearing seat off and raises the heavy seat to 15.0 kN (crippling 0.90).
should_fix.fix: Draw the cradle and the head with every hole in place. For example: deeper cheeks with the strap bolts below the bearing bolts and a spacer that clears the bolt heads; at the head, straps outside the cheeks with a bolt group above the truss whose lines pass through the pin. State that the strap line of action is at or below the chord underside. Re-check bearing, tear-out, edge distances, the seat split and the landing height.

should_fix.title: Cradle seat crippling uses a formula outside its test basis
should_fix.evidence: run_connectors.py:35-39 and 101 use the AISI S100-16 G5 C-section coefficients (C 13, CR 0.23, CN 0.14, Ch 0.01) and treat the chord's two flanges as the webs (h 36, N 40, t 1.15). Reproduced: 9,290 N per flange, 16.72 kN for both, against 12.95 kN = 0.77. In the G5 tests the load passes through a web between two flanges. Here each chord flange has only a 9 mm lip on its far edge, and that lip is notched away right over the packer. The force also leaves the flange at mid-height, through 2 screws into the nested web. The parameters are in range; the edge conditions are not.
should_fix.fix: Find the seat capacity by testing a 1.15 mm chord joint pair with nested webs, for both the screwed and the bearing-only seat, and put the test factor and acceptance into H4. Until then, treat the 0.77 as unverified.

should_fix.title: Strap net-section check leaves out the bolted thin-sheet net-section rule
should_fix.evidence: run_connectors.py:66 and 75 (connectors.py:43-46) take 0.65 An fu with full efficiency: 13.48 kN for 50 x 1.2 and 16.85 kN for 50 x 1.5, utilisation 0.58 / 0.55. The bolted thin-sheet rule (AISI S100-07 E3.2 form) is lower. With washers, (0.1 + 3d/s) An fu = 0.82 An fu at phi 0.55, giving 9.35 / 11.69 kN: utilisation 0.84 for the south A-frame strap (7.84 kN per strap) and 0.79 for the north hanger (9.26 kN). Without washers, 2.5d/s = 0.60 at phi 0.65 gives 0.97 / 0.92. Still below 1.0, but with much less margin than reported.
should_fix.fix: Confirm the AS/NZS 4600:2018 clause 5.3.3 values (net-section efficiency and phi in single shear) from the licensed text. Specify washers under the head and the nut of every strap bolt. Update the check.

should_fix.title: Reported margins sit inside the uncertainty of the link and joint idealisation
should_fix.evidence: Re-run sensitivity over the design cases. Links 4 times stiffer (link_I 800, about 28 kN/mm): W4 bottom track 1.03, link shear 0.82. Links 4 times softer (link_I 50, about 1.7 kN/mm): T2 tie tension 6.56 kN against 6.37 kN capacity (1.03; reported 5.75 kN, 0.90), joints 0.93. In-plane joint fixity 0.3: members 0.99. The 235 gussets make many joints semi-rigid, but they are modelled only as extra screw capacity on joints that stay pinned.
should_fix.fix: Run bounding cases (link stiffness x0.25 and x4, joint fixity 0 to 0.5) and design for their envelope. Or justify the 7 kN/mm link stiffness by test for the actual screw and ply combination. Model the gusseted joints with rotational stiffness.

should_fix.title: The in-service check assumes a support and a mass that the hold points do not deliver
should_fix.evidence: run_service.py:115-118 holds every edge-truss bottom-chord node rigidly. The landing rule allows bearers within +/-2 mm, packed between the cradles (review.json:73). Re-run: base case 0.949 / 0.895 / 0.80, as reported. With one 1.2 m length unsupported on the south side (x 5400-6600), the NFT13 bottom chord reaches 1.095, while the edge truss deflects only 0.29 mm (SLS) / 0.52 mm (ULS) across that length. A packer 0.3-0.5 mm low there therefore never comes into contact. With 1.8 m unsupported on both sides: members 1.07, joints 1.31 (NFT2 web at x 6908), 9 joints over. On the mass: run_service.py:96 uses the itemised 4,652 kg, but H1 accepts up to 6,500/1.03 = 6,311 kg; at that mass the NFT4 bottom and top chords reach 1.022 and 1.018.
should_fix.fix: Put a packer directly under every floor-truss end (600 mm centres) and under each joint pair outside the cradles, and shim each to full bearing after set-down, checked with a feeler gauge. Otherwise analyse the real support (springs with +/-2 mm offsets). Apply the same rule to storage and to the foundation. Re-run the service check with the weighed mass and the distribution from the 8 H1 readings.

should_fix.title: 172 of the 235 gussets are permanent floor structure booked as lift parts, and were sized against an ideal support
should_fix.evidence: results/joint_schedule.json gives 172 gussets source 'service' and 63 source 'lift'. The 172 are floor-truss web joints on NFT3-NFT23 with 4-screw utilisation up to 1.38. size_joints.py:35-41 sized them from service_joint_demands on rigid bearers, to a 0.90 limit. results/framer_components/summary.json books all 235 as LIFT_GU 'lift parts'. So the floor cassette as framed does not carry a 3 kPa classroom floor without them, and under a realistic support other joints exceed 1.0 (NFT2 web 1.31 in the 1.8 m case).
should_fix.fix: Give the service gussets their own component and BOQ code, and show them on the floor-cassette shop drawings. State in the basis that they are needed whether or not the module is lifted. Re-size them against the real packer layout, or fix the floor truss itself (gauge, web layout or screws).

should_fix.title: Framer gauge step: the 1.15 mm trusses exist only in the script, and the release and clash checks cover less than reported
should_fix.evidence: add_lift_components.py:163-173 re-gauges NFT1, NFT2 and NFT25 after framing and calls modelling.regenerate, which is Framer's own tooling. But model/engineered/project_with_lift_parts.json has no profile or gauge setting, only a free-text note. A release from the saved job would therefore roll these lift-critical trusses at the default 0.95 mm. Lines 182-183 call the release check with run_clash=False and a test-only orphan tolerance. Framer's release_gate.py:404 then warns 'TEST-ONLY - enter the real value before a production release', and summary.json does not record that warning. Line 181 passes only the frame panels to clash detection, and Framer's clash.py has no component handling at all. So '0 clashes' covers frame members only; the 603 lift parts were never clash-checked. The build reviewer also found that a truss framed at 1.15 mm has webs 0.40-0.47 mm shorter (not re-run here).
should_fix.fix: Put the gauge where Framer frames from: frame the three trusses as a separate job with settings.profile C89-38-1.15, or frame the whole module at 1.15 mm. Record the release-check warnings in the summary. Add a hold point for the 1.15 mm coil certificate and the panel labels. Clash-check the lift parts outside Framer.

should_fix.title: Marriage-face hardware stands 15-30 mm proud, not within 12 mm, and faces the second module's hardware
should_fix.evidence: review.json:97 says everything on the marriage face is within 12 mm, and sets a 15 mm gap. With standard ISO hardware: cradle cheek plus M16 head and washer, 16 mm (about 24 mm on the nut side); strap, cheek and M12 head with washer, about 14.5 mm (about 21 mm on the nut side); at the head, 3 mm clearance plus 3 mm cheek plus 1.5 mm strap plus M12 head and washer, about 17.5 mm. The 120 mm pin ends 15.5 mm past the truss face before its head or nut, and about 30 mm with an M20 nut. should_fix.title: Lift straps must stay free between their end bolts
should_fix.evidence: Each strap pair is modelled as one pinned member from the cradle to the head, with nothing attached in between (run_lift.py:295-297 and 326-328). On both faces the straps cross studs, noggins, plates and chords, under battens, linings and the floor sheet. Screwing linings or battens through a strap would put lift load into lining and batten screws, which is not modelled.
should_fix.fix: Add a detailing rule and an inspection hold point: no fixings through lift straps; battens packed or set out past the straps; linings fixed clear of them; the floor sheet and ceiling notched; tie plates moved off the strap paths.

should_fix.title: Plane-bracing strap ends are still under the wall bottom tracks and inside the roof saddles (Rev C finding not answered)
should_fix.evidence: The bracing stations are x 0, 900, 4500, 7500, 11100 and 12000, at z -20.5 (floor) and 2979.5 (roof), on the edge-truss top chords (revD_final.json:41-74). All 12 floor strap ends lie under a wall bottom track: EW1 runs the full length on the south, and the returns and piers cover them on the north. 8 of the 12 roof strap ends lie inside a saddle footprint (lift line +/-60 mm). The Rev C review raised this (results/review/reviews.json:503), and review.json has no resolution for it. The bracing is essential (the Rev C ablation without it was near a mechanism).
should_fix.fix: Anchor the bracing 150-300 mm away from the lift lines and wall lines, on the inside face or on the first truss with a small plate. Use wafer heads under tracks and put tensioners only where there is room. Re-run, because the bracing stations change.

notes: The cradle seat model is fair. Every seat stays in compression in every design case (0.86-12.96 kN factored), and the A-frame split at S2 matches statics at the apex (11.67/11.04 kN in the model against 11.67/11.06 by statics). The split between the two seats depends on the strap-bolt height, which is not yet fixed (see the strap-bolt finding).

A lifted-off bearing seat keeps 1e-3 of its area (run_lift.py:384), which acts as a 3.9 kN/mm spring and is then the cradle's only in-plane rotational restraint. _unilateral gives no warning at max_iter. No effect in Rev D, because no seat lifts off in a design case.

The saddle model carries no vertical load: 0.03 kN against a 22.5 kN head force. The load split between the two straps of a pair is set by fit-up, not statics: in 14 mm holes, a 2 mm length difference shifts 6.9-8.7 kN. State a fit-up rule (match-drilled, both faces snug before lifting) or check a 70/30 split.
